newsitem.title: USA: Domenici says Clinton must lead on CPI changes.
newsitem.headline: Domenici says Clinton must lead on CPI changes.

text.p: A top Senate Republican said on Sunday he saw no possiblity of changing the Consumer Price Index (CPI) unless President Bill Clinton took the lead on the matter.

"I believe it is impossible to objectively analyze and change ... the CPI, if that is necessary, without the leadership of the president," Senator Pete Domenici, a New Mexico Republican, said on CNN's Late Edition program.

Domenici, the chairman of the Senate budget committee, was adding his voice to that of the House Budget Committe chairman John Kasich, an Ohio Republican, who told NBC Television on Sunday that Clinton must move first on the matter.
The question of who takes the lead on changing the CPI is politically sensitive because of its role in adjusting key benefits, like the social security retirement program, for inflation.

Republicans, who control both houses of Congress, have argued that the president must take the initiative essentially because they do not want to take the blame for the possible resulting reduction in benefits.
Last week a commission chaired by Stanford economist Michael Boskin released a report arguing that the CPI overstates inflation by 1.1 percentage points per year and recommending a series of changes.
Any changes would have a huge impact on the federal budget because of the many index-linked benefit payments.
